mission: Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.

stage2a.operation: ChAT/neuronal substrate supply is distinct from PC membrane biosynthesis. B5/folate context and shared-pool claims are retained but not promoted.

existing_findings.proposition: Sodium-coupled high-affinity choline uptake through CHT/SLC5A7 is required to recover choline into cholinergic nerve terminals and commonly limits acetylcholine production under physiological demand.

existing_source_assessments.label: Ojiakor and Rylett (2020)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: CHT-mediated high-affinity choline uptake recovers choline into cholinergic terminals and is the principal regulated supply step for sustaining acetylcholine production.

assessment.study: Review of CHT function, trafficking, genetic disruption, and pharmacological manipulation.
assessment.population: Cellular, animal, human genetic, and neuropathology evidence; not a dietary trial.
assessment.result: Reduced CHT function or availability limits choline uptake and cholinergic transmission, while neuronal activity recruits transport capacity.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the regulated choline-entry step required before acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.limitations: Does not test ordinary food intake or human brain synthesis after a meal.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Inazu (2019)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Separates CTL1/CTL2-mediated choline handling at brain microvascular endothelium from CHT/SLC5A7 uptake at cholinergic terminals.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not test whether an oral choline exposure increases delivery to terminals or acetylcholine synthesis in humans.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Acetylcholine is formed from choline and acetyl-CoA by choline acetyltransferase; biochemical necessity is not intake-responsive human brain acetylcholine.

existing_source_assessments.label: Oda (1999)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Choline acetyltransferase condenses choline and acetyl-CoA to form acetylcholine and is the defining synthetic enzyme in cholinergic neurons.

assessment.study: Review of choline-acetyltransferase structure, distribution and pathology.
assessment.population: Experimental and neuropathology literature; not a dietary sample.
assessment.result: Identified choline and acetyl-CoA as the enzyme’s substrates.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.limitations: Enzyme and pathology review; not an intake-to-acetylcholine trial.

existing_source_assessments.label: Ojiakor and Rylett (2020)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: ChAT transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to choline in the neuronal cytoplasm after CHT-mediated choline entry.

assessment.study: Review of CHT function and cholinergic terminal biology.
assessment.population: Mechanistic, animal, and human genetic literature.
assessment.result: Describes substrate entry followed by ChAT-dependent synthesis from choline and acetyl-CoA.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independently confirms the reaction participants within the presynaptic synthesis pathway.
assessment.limitations: Does not measure human synthesis after dietary exposure.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Kennedy (2016)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews B-vitamin roles in brain energy and one-carbon chemistry.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Does not establish vitamin B12 or folate as acetylcholine-synthesis cofactors.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Dietary phosphatidylcholine is digested and remodelled into circulating phosphatidylcholine and free choline, establishing a dietary provision route to the direct choline substrate.

existing_source_assessments.label: Böckmann et al. (2023)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Oral labelled phosphatidylcholine produced delayed circulating labelled choline and the highest labelled phosphatidylcholine exposure among four tested choline forms.

assessment.study: Randomized crossover stable-isotope comparison of four oral choline forms.
assessment.result: Phosphatidylcholine was digested and remodelled, with delayed plasma choline appearance and higher plasma phosphatidylcholine exposure.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Delayed choline peak and approximately 2.3-fold higher peak labelled phosphatidylcholine than water-soluble forms.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes phosphatidylcholine as an assimilated choline-provision route.
assessment.limitations: Small sample; supplement bolus rather than whole food; no brain or acetylcholine measurement.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Pantothenate supports acetylcholine-synthesis capacity through coenzyme A and acetyl-CoA formation, and severe chronic pantothenate depletion can reduce brain acetylcholine synthesis in rats.

existing_source_assessments.label: Rivera-Calimlim et al. (1988)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Chronic ethanol depleted rat-brain pantothenate and inhibited acetylcholine synthesis, while pantothenate co-administration increased both brain pantothenate and synthesis.

assessment.study: Chronic and acute ethanol exposure with or without oral pantothenate in rats, measuring labelled acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.result: The chronic four-month condition reduced brain pantothenate and acetylcholine synthesis; pantothenate co-treatment partly restored both.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Brain pantothenate fell to 7% of control with chronic ethanol; synthesis differences were statistically significant but no transferable human effect size is available.
assessment.evidence_summary: Directly links severe pantothenate depletion to reduced acetylcholine synthesis through acetyl-CoA provision.
assessment.limitations: Ethanol-specific animal model, very high pantothenate doses, and no ordinary-diet or human outcome.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Inadequate folate-dependent or B12-dependent methionine-cycle capacity can disturb brain choline metabolism and lower acetylcholine availability, creating a supported shared-resource constraint on acetylcholine-synthesis capacity.

existing_source_assessments.label: Chan et al. (2008)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Dietary folate compromise lowered mouse-brain choline and acetylcholine, while SAM supplementation under folate deficiency restored both pools.

assessment.study: Dietary folate deficiency across adult, aged, and genetically susceptible mouse models with SAM rescue.
assessment.population: Mice of several genotypes and ages.
assessment.result: Folate compromise reduced choline and acetylcholine; SAM restored these measures and cognitive performance in the deficient condition.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Directionally consistent rescue across several mouse contexts; no human effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the link from one-carbon donor insufficiency to loss of the choline resource used for acetylcholine.
assessment.limitations: Mixed dietary, oxidative, age, and genotype contexts; pool concentrations rather than direct synthesis flux.

existing_source_assessments.label: Jadavji et al. (2014)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Methionine-synthase-reductase-deficient mice had lower hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine with compensatory ChAT and AChE expression changes.

assessment.study: Genetic mouse model of impaired methionine synthase reductase.
assessment.result: Deficiency reduced hippocampal choline, betaine, and acetylcholine and impaired short-term memory.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Significant group differences reported; no dietary or human effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Adds B12-dependent methionine-cycle evidence to the shared-resource constraint.
assessment.limitations: Genetic mouse model; altered concentration and enzyme expression do not quantify synthesis flux.

existing_source_assessments.label: Crivello et al. (2010)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Ten weeks of folate deficiency changed brain acetylcholine in adult rats by region—lower in hippocampus but higher in cortex and striatum—with little brain effect in young rats.

assessment.study: Controlled folate-deficient versus control diets in young and adult male rats.
assessment.population: Male Sprague Dawley rats starting at four weeks or nine months.
assessment.result: Brain choline and acetylcholine responses depended on age and region rather than moving uniformly.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Significant regional differences; no whole-brain or human synthesis estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Qualifies the constraint as context-dependent and prevents a universal lower-acetylcholine claim.
assessment.limitations: Concentrations rather than synthesis flux; animal model; mixed regional direction.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Cytosolic acetyl-CoA for acetylcholine synthesis is supplied through compartmented neuronal metabolism, and its availability can regulate synthesis independently of choline transport.

existing_source_assessments.label: Jope (1979)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Acetyl-CoA availability may limit acetylcholine synthesis, with evidence for citrate-lyase, pyruvate-dehydrogenase, and mitochondrial export routes supplying the cytosolic reaction.

assessment.study: Review of high-affinity choline transport, acetyl-CoA production, compartmentation, and regulation of brain acetylcholine synthesis.
assessment.population: Biochemical, synaptosomal, and animal literature; no dietary human trial.
assessment.result: Distinguished mitochondrial acetyl-CoA generation from cytosolic use by ChAT and identified several supported supply routes.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes compartmented acetyl-CoA provision as a second upstream substrate-control problem.
assessment.limitations: Older mechanistic literature; the relative contribution of proposed routes remains context-dependent.

existing_supportive_evidence.label: Szutowicz et al. (2010)
existing_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Pyrithiamine-induced thiamine deficiency reduced pyruvate-dehydrogenase flux and mitochondrial and cytosolic acetyl-CoA in rat nerve terminals, supporting the compartmented acetyl-unit supply model.
existing_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: The reported cholinergic endpoint was altered quantal acetylcholine release, while ChAT activity was unchanged; it does not establish vitamin B1 as a PM6 synthesis requirement or intake-responsive lever.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: Human ADHD-related muscarinic-binding and choline-status evidence is translationally relevant to attention; it is not a demonstration that changing choline intake treats ADHD.

existing_source_assessments.label: Johansson et al. (2013)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Decreased muscarinic binding in boys with ADHD supplies attention-relevant cholinergic context, not a treatment effect.

assessment.study: Same fibroblast binding comparison used in PM6-F1, reused here for the attention relationship.
assessment.population: Boys with ADHD and comparison boys.
assessment.result: Lower muscarinic binding in the ADHD group.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Binding contrast only; no attention-score change after diet.
assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the attention relationship in human cholinergic biology.
assessment.limitations: Not brain imaging of acetylcholine and not a dietary trial.

existing_source_assessments.label: Derbyshire and Maes (2023)
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Altered choline status is discussed in ADHD-related literature without proving choline treatment of ADHD.

assessment.study: Same narrative review used in PM6-F1 and PM6-F2, reused here for phenome context.
assessment.population: ADHD and other neurodevelopmental subgroups summarised in the review.
assessment.result: Discussed choline as a possible modifiable neurodevelopmental factor.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supplies choline-status context for attention, not a dosing rule.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; not a choline-for-ADHD trial.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

The ethanol-specific pantothenate experiment does not isolate a simple dietary deficiency or prove the proposed mediator.

preserved_phenome_source_records.rationale: Acetylcholine is the cholinergic transmitter used in attention and learning circuits {{cite:johansson_decreased_2013}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. Receptor-binding differences in boys with ADHD and choline/neurodevelopment reviews supply translational context. They do not show that changing choline intake treats ADHD or raises brain acetylcholine.

Cholinergic signalling is a biological context for working-memory and cognitive precision {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}} {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. The attached sources do not measure cognitive-clarity scores after a choline change aimed at acetylcholine synthesis.

stage2b.clarification: Retain choline, phosphatidylcholine, acetyl-CoA, B5 and folate records in their accepted categories, including those not selected in the rapid manuscript. Phosphatidylcholine is a precursor route to choline, not a second independent acetylcholine effect.

section_presentations.label: Choline
section_presentations.reader_description: Choline is the starting material transported into cholinergic nerve endings and joined to acetyl-CoA to make acetylcholine.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Choline is the Direct substrate for choline-acetyltransferase formation of acetylcholine. Diet supplies choline, but this is not an acetylcholine-dosing or attention-treatment rule.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Choline is required and diet supplies it, but additional intake has not been shown here to raise acetylcholine synthesis in the human brain or improve attention.

all_existing_inputs.preservation_note: The rapid manuscript selection is not the canonical inventory. Absence from that selection changes no accepted status or source record.

section_presentations.label: Phosphatidylcholine
section_presentations.reader_description: Phosphatidylcholine is digested and remodelled as a choline-containing food form. It provides choline rather than acting as a second substrate in the synthesis reaction.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Phosphatidylcholine is a Derived Dietary Requirement because digestion and remodelling provide choline. It is a provision route, not a second acetylcholine-synthesis substrate.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Human tracer evidence establishes phosphatidylcholine as a choline-provision route; it does not show delivery to cholinergic terminals or increased brain acetylcholine synthesis.

all_existing_inputs.preservation_note: The rapid manuscript selection is not the canonical inventory. Absence from that selection changes no accepted status or source record.

section_presentations.label: Acetyl-CoA
section_presentations.reader_description: Acetyl-CoA is generated through compartmented neuronal metabolism and donates the acetyl group used by choline acetyltransferase.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Acetyl-CoA is the second biochemical substrate used by choline acetyltransferase. It is generated inside cells and is not a dietary acetyl-CoA target.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Acetyl-CoA is a cellular reaction substrate, not a dietary acetyl-CoA recommendation; ordinary dietary control of its availability in human cholinergic neurons is not established.

all_existing_inputs.preservation_note: The rapid manuscript selection is not the canonical inventory. Absence from that selection changes no accepted status or source record.

section_presentations.label: Vitamin B5 (pantothenate)
section_presentations.reader_description: Pantothenate is used to make coenzyme A, which cells use to form acetyl-CoA—the second substrate in acetylcholine synthesis.

type_delivery_metadata.permitted_wording: Vitamin B5 supplies pantothenate for coenzyme A and acetyl-CoA formation. It is a biochemical precursor relationship, not a direct ChAT cofactor.
type_delivery_metadata.evidence_limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.
